title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 63131033.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 72130631.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.

GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 43121355.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 43161116.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 43291049.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 43370933.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

pds:Field_Binary.pds:description: A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag associated with frequency counter readings in Fields 20 and 21, in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This is the FTS time at which the program stored the FMS phases described in fields 20 and 21. This time tag is for diagnostic purposes only.
A composite field containing predict time offset enter by the operator in days and seconds within a day.

Filter Offset; the value used by software to tune the carrier signal to center of the filter. This offset compensates for the unique characteristics and placement of the filter in the RF spectrum. The value is a 32-bit signed binary, scaled in Hertz; it is applied to the predict set frequencies to obtain the final frequency result for the POCA. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 43391217.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.

GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 20240215.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 1, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 20390434.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.

GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 32901112.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

pds:Field_Binary.pds:description: A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag associated with frequency counter readings in Fields 20 and 21, in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This is the FTS time at which the program stored the FMS phases described in fields 20 and 21. This time tag is for diagnostic purposes only.
A composite field containing predict time offset enter by the operator in days and seconds within a day.

Filter Offset; the value used by software to tune the carrier signal to center of the filter. This offset compensates for the unique characteristics and placement of the filter in the RF spectrum. The value is a 32-bit signed binary, scaled in Hertz; it is applied to the predict set frequencies to obtain the final frequency result for the POCA. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33020812.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

pds:Field_Binary.pds:description: A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag associated with frequency counter readings in Fields 20 and 21, in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This is the FTS time at which the program stored the FMS phases described in fields 20 and 21. This time tag is for diagnostic purposes only.
A composite field containing predict time offset enter by the operator in days and seconds within a day.

Filter Offset; the value used by software to tune the carrier signal to center of the filter. This offset compensates for the unique characteristics and placement of the filter in the RF spectrum. The value is a 32-bit signed binary, scaled in Hertz; it is applied to the predict set frequencies to obtain the final frequency result for the POCA. NOTES: 1. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33031955.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33080730.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

pds:Field_Binary.pds:description: A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag associated with frequency counter readings in Fields 20 and 21, in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This is the FTS time at which the program stored the FMS phases described in fields 20 and 21. This time tag is for diagnostic purposes only.
A composite field containing predict time offset enter by the operator in days and seconds within a day.

Filter Offset; the value used by software to tune the carrier signal to center of the filter. This offset compensates for the unique characteristics and placement of the filter in the RF spectrum. The value is a 32-bit signed binary, scaled in Hertz; it is applied to the predict set frequencies to obtain the final frequency result for the POCA. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33082001.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2.
