GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.
Day of year, from the Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS). Jan 1 = 1.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).
Flag denoting manual or computer control of the POCA. Set to 0 if POCA is under COMPUTER control* 1 if POCA is under MANUAL control
Flag denoting whether the POCA is ready. Set to 0 if NOT READY 1 if READY*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer power is on. Set to 0 if synthesizer power is OFF 1 if synthesizer power is ON*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

The 'calculated' POCA frequency in binary coded decimal (BCD); the value of the predicted frequency (plus filter offset and operator- entered offset) interpolated by the DSP-R for the time recorded in Field 14. The predicted frequency is supplied by the NSS Radio Science prediction software and is used primarily for diagnostic purposes; values in Field 13 should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects requested configuration of the IF-video switch (operator input selection). Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects configuration of the IF-video switch as reported by the IF switch assembly. Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)
Four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. The following are examples of POCA rates: Byte 52 Bytes 53-54 Decimal Rate Conversion (hex) (hex) (Hz/sec) ------- ----------- ----------------------- 12 3452 -1.2345 12 3457 123.45 12 3451 0.12345
The mantissa of the POCA frequency rate as read from the POCA rate registers (5 BCD digits following the decimal point -- e.g., 0.12345).
Power of ten multiplier for the mantissa contained in bits 1-20. For example, binary 011 in bits 21-23 means the mantissa should be multiplied by 1000.
Sign of the POCA rate. Set to 0 if the POCA rate is negative 1 if the POCA rate is positive

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 1, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 2, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.
A set of three four-bit and four one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Frequency Monitoring Subsystem (FMS). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

Second bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating whether test samples have been enabled to the counter. Set to 1 if test sample to counter is ENABLED* 0 if test sample to counter is DISABLED
Third bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating the source of 10 MHz to resolvers. Set to 1 to enable INTERNAL 10 MHz to resolvers* 0 to enable REFERENCE 10 MHz to resolvers
Fourth bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating to source of 10 MHZ to test facilities. Set to 1 to enable INTERNAL 10 MHz to test facilities* 0 to enable REFERENCE 10 MHz to test facilities
Frequency Counter No. 1 Mode Register. Set to 0000 for Test Facility output to counter 0001 for live frequency to counter (POCA)*
Frequency Counter No. 2 Mode Register. Set to 0000 for Test Facility output to counter 0001 for live frequency to counter (POCA)*

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 20262100.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Field_Bit.pds:description: The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.
Day of year, from the Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS). Jan 1 = 1.

Flag denoting whether the POCA is ready. Set to 0 if NOT READY 1 if READY*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer power is on. Set to 0 if synthesizer power is OFF 1 if synthesizer power is ON*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

The 'calculated' POCA frequency in binary coded decimal (BCD); the value of the predicted frequency (plus filter offset and operator- entered offset) interpolated by the DSP-R for the time recorded in Field 14. The predicted frequency is supplied by the NSS Radio Science prediction software and is used primarily for diagnostic purposes; values in Field 13 should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects requested configuration of the IF-video switch (operator input selection). Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects configuration of the IF-video switch as reported by the IF switch assembly. Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)
Four unused bits.
The mantissa of the POCA frequency rate as read from the POCA rate registers (5 BCD digits following the decimal point -- e.g., 0.12345).
Power of ten multiplier for the mantissa contained in bits 1-20. For example, binary 011 in bits 21-23 means the mantissa should be multiplied by 1000.
Sign of the POCA rate. Set to 0 if the POCA rate is negative 1 if the POCA rate is positive

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 1, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 2, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 20411159.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.
Day of year, from the Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS). Jan 1 = 1.

Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).

Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

The 'calculated' POCA frequency in binary coded decimal (BCD); the value of the predicted frequency (plus filter offset and operator- entered offset) interpolated by the DSP-R for the time recorded in Field 14. The predicted frequency is supplied by the NSS Radio Science prediction software and is used primarily for diagnostic purposes; values in Field 13 should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 1, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 32941741.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33020812.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
Prime Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8.
Secondary Front End Area, or antenna, (FEA) number (e.g., 14, 43). FEA assignments are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. Set to 0 if only one antenna was used.

Spacecraft number. Spacecraft number assignments are given in Tables OPS-6-8-10 and OPS-6-8-10A of DSN document OPS-6-8 For example: Magellan 18 Voyager 1 31 Voyager 2 32 Clementine 64 Galileo Orbiter 77
Signal Processing Center (SPC) designator. SPC designators are given in the fourth field of Table OPS-6-8-6 of DSN document OPS-6-8. For example: Goldstone 10 Canberra 40 Madrid 60
two-digit year and day of year.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.
Day of year, from the Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS). Jan 1 = 1.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (and typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give time of the first sample in the record (row) in milliseconds past 0 hours Universal Time Coordinated (UTC). Only guaranteed accurate when the flag in Field 1, bit 1 is set to 1.
Predict Set ID; an identifier for the set of predicts used to tune the open-loop receiver. Ten 8-bit ASCII characters.
A set of eight one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Programmable Oscillator Control Assembly (POCA). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).
Flag denoting manual or computer control of the POCA. Set to 0 if POCA is under COMPUTER control* 1 if POCA is under MANUAL control
Flag denoting whether the POCA is ready. Set to 0 if NOT READY 1 if READY*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer power is on. Set to 0 if synthesizer power is OFF 1 if synthesizer power is ON*
Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (but typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the actual FTS time read from the POCA register in milliseconds past O h UTC. This is the time value that should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency values.
Eight unused bits.

The 'calculated' POCA frequency in binary coded decimal (BCD); the value of the predicted frequency (plus filter offset and operator- entered offset) interpolated by the DSP-R for the time recorded in Field 14. The predicted frequency is supplied by the NSS Radio Science prediction software and is used primarily for diagnostic purposes; values in Field 13 should be used for reconstructing POCA frequency. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag of the POCA frequency update cycle in milliseconds past O h UTC. This time value is for diagnostic purposes only, and should not be used for data reconstruction.
A pair of two-bit flags indicating configuration of the IF-video switch selection, followed by four unused bits.

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects requested configuration of the IF-video switch (operator input selection). Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)

Antenna RF configuration code which reflects configuration of the IF-video switch as reported by the IF switch assembly. Modes used are: 01 = PRIME mode (70 m) 10 = CROSS mode (34 m HEF) 11 = FAROT mode (Faraday rotation)
Four unused bits.

Rate at which the POCA frequency changes given as a BCD mantissa, a power-of-ten multiplier, and a sign bit. The following are examples of POCA rates: Byte 52 Bytes 53-54 Decimal Rate Conversion (hex) (hex) (Hz/sec) ------- ----------- ----------------------- 12 3452 -1.2345 12 3457 123.45 12 3451 0.12345
The mantissa of the POCA frequency rate as read from the POCA rate registers (5 BCD digits following the decimal point -- e.g., 0.12345).
Power of ten multiplier for the mantissa contained in bits 1-20. For example, binary 011 in bits 21-23 means the mantissa should be multiplied by 1000.
Sign of the POCA rate. Set to 0 if the POCA rate is negative 1 if the POCA rate is positive

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 1, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.

One-second accumulated phase from frequency counter No. 2, scaled to 2^-20 cycles. The last 20 bits are the fractional part of one cycle. This is a 'running count,' not the difference count from the previous second.
A set of three four-bit and four one-bit flags indicating status and configuration of the Frequency Monitoring Subsystem (FMS). Normal radio science use is indicated with an asterisk (*).
FMS Test Facility input signal selection. Set to 0001 for live input of Counter 1 (POCA 'J1')* 0010 for live input of Counter 2 ('J2', not used)"

First bit from the FMS Sample Control Register, indicating whether live samples have been enabled to the counter. Set to 1 if live sample to counter is ENABLED* 0 if live sample to counter is DISABLED
Second bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating whether test samples have been enabled to the counter. Set to 1 if test sample to counter is ENABLED* 0 if test sample to counter is DISABLED
Third bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating the source of 10 MHz to resolvers. Set to 1 to enable INTERNAL 10 MHz to resolvers* 0 to enable REFERENCE 10 MHz to resolvers
Fourth bit from FMS Sample Control Register, indicating to source of 10 MHZ to test facilities. Set to 1 to enable INTERNAL 10 MHz to test facilities* 0 to enable REFERENCE 10 MHz to test facilities
Frequency Counter No. 1 Mode Register. Set to 0000 for Test Facility output to counter 0001 for live frequency to counter (POCA)*
Frequency Counter No. 2 Mode Register. Set to 0000 for Test Facility output to counter 0001 for live frequency to counter (POCA)*

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 contain the time tag associated with frequency counter readings in Fields 20 and 21, in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This is the FTS time at which the program stored the FMS phases described in fields 20 and 21. This time tag is for diagnostic purposes only.
A composite field containing predict time offset enter by the operator in days and seconds within a day.
Predict Time offset in days (positive value)
Five unused bits
Sign of the Predict Time Offset; this sign is applied to both the days and seconds portions of the offset. Set to 1 for negative offsets 0 for positive offsets

Predict Time Offset in seconds. This time offset is input by the operator in real time as a last-minute correction to the time domain of the predict set. This value is added to the predict set times, and the results are tracked relative to real (current) FTS. Therefore, positive time offsets will cause the original predict times to occur later, and negative values cause the times to occur earlier.

The S-band Frequency Offset to the predict set; formatted as a 48-bit binary number with least significant bit equal to 2^-20 Hz. Value may be positive or negative (2's complement format). Maximum value is 2 MHz. This Frequency Offset value is entered by the operator in real time as a last-minute correction to the frequency domain of the predict set.

Filter Offset; the value used by software to tune the carrier signal to center of the filter. This offset compensates for the unique characteristics and placement of the filter in the RF spectrum. The value is a 32-bit signed binary, scaled in Hertz; it is applied to the predict set frequencies to obtain the final frequency result for the POCA. NOTE: The following station-dependent formulas are used to determine POCA settings: POCA = 2*(Fs - 300 - FO)/9 - 400 (DSS 7 and 42) POCA = (Fs - 300 - FO)/48 (DSS 12 and 61) POCA = (Fs - FO)/3 - 721 - 9/11 (all other stations) where POCA = POCA frequency (MHz) Fs = S-Band value (MHz) FO = Filter Offset (MHz) (Field 26) The offsets found in Fields 24 and 25 are applied to Fs before these formulas are used.

Receiver Channel 1 root mean square voltage as reported by the Radio Science IF-VF Converter Assembly (RIV) Controller.

Maximum AD value found in calculating the RMS reported in Field 47. In 12-bit sampling, this field holds the most significant 8 bits of the maximum sample value.
Minimum AD value found in calculating the RMS reported in Field 47. In 12-bit sampling, this field holds the most significant 8 bits of the minimum sample value.

A composite field in which bits 1-5 are unused (typically set to 0) and bits 6-32 give the time tag for NBOC buffer samples used to calculate RMS voltages (Fields 47-50) and obtain maximum and minimum sample values (Fields 51-66); in milliseconds past 0 hours UTC. This time tag corresponds to the time tag found in Field 10 of an earlier tape record (table row). The AD data from this earlier record (row) were saved to run the calculations found in Fields 47-50 of this (current) record.

Sample rate; number of samples per second from a single analog-to-digital (AD) converter (the number of samples per second per AD converter is given in the first field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).
First two bytes of the six bytes of sync data received from NBOC at the beginning of each second. Value should be A55A in hex or 42330 in decimal.
This 16-bit field is reserved for diagnostic use.
A set of one- and two-bit flags giving the status and configuration of the NBOC as reported in the Conversion Mode Register.
One-bit flag indicating whether an NBOC converter overflow occurred. Set to 1 if an NBOC converter overflow occurred 0 if nominal
Unused bit.
One-bit flag indicating whether the NBOC phase-lock loop is in lock. Set to 1 if NBOC PLL in lock 0 if NBOC PLL out of lock
One-bit flag indicating whether sampling is at 'high' or 'low' rate. Set to 1 for 50-, 20-, 10-, 5-, and 2-ksps rates 0 for 1000- and 200 samples/second rates
One-bit flag indicating indicating whether the NBOC is in test mode. Set to 1 for test mode 0 for normal operational mode
One-bit flag indicating whether 8-bit or 12-bit samples are being taken. Set to 1 for 8-bit resolution 0 for 12-bit resolution

Mode. Various combinations of input signals and AD assignments are possible. Four modes have been defined as follows: 00 4 input signals, each sampled by a separate converter 01 1 input signal sampled sequentially by 4 AD converters 10 2 input signals, each sampled sequentially by 2 AD converters 11 1 signal sampled sequentially by 3 AD converters NOTE: The MODE assignments here and the mode numbers appearing in documentation and procedure documents usually differ by 1. That is, 'mode 1' has a field value 00.

Assignments of receiver channels to AD converters. In conjunction with the MODE in Field 71, these map receiver channels into sample fields in the data portion of each record (table row). Example: if bits 1-8 equal 10101010, then all four AD converters will sample receiver channel 3.

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33031955.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33082001.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.
Day of year, from the Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS). Jan 1 = 1.

Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. A composite field in which the first four bits are one-bit flags and the last four bits are a single flag.

The origin of the Narrow Band Occultation Converter (NBOC) time tag (Field 10) and configuration information (Fields 69 through 72). Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. Cycling between these two modes will cause each tape to be labeled No. 1, in which case the tape sequence must be determined from the time tag in Field 10. During auto-start/stop operations, the BEGIN RECORDING and END RECORDING directives do not alter the Tape Number.
Record number within the file (row number within the table); reset to 1 at the beginning of each file/table).
Record length; number of 16-bit words per record (the number of words per record is given in the fifth field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33140800.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.

Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985
pds:Citation_Information.pds:description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission

description: DSN Original Data Record RSC-11-11 file produced for Galileo mission
Galileo ODR labeled in PDS4, original product 33141610.ODR
GLL raw open-loop data

Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. Tape Number in this recording session; first tape is No. 1. NOTE: A new recording session is indicated each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN. NOTES: 1. If bit 1 is set to '1' the following additional validity checks may be made: (a) Field 69 should be 'A55A' (b) Fields 71 and 72 should indicate the correct configuration from the Conversion Mode Register. 2. After bit 1 is set to '1' it will read '0' for the next L-1 records (table rows), where L is the number of records per second (the number of records per second is given in the third field of Table 1 in DSN document RSC-11-11).

Flag indicating start of a recording session. Set to 0 if other than first record in the recording session. 1 if this is the first record of the recording session. NOTE: Each time the program mode is changed from IDLE to RUN, this bit is set to 1 in the first record. When the software is in its auto- start/stop operating mode, this bit is set to 1 in the first record after a BEGIN RECORDING directive is processed from the active predict set.

Flag signaling error during tape copy process. This flag will never be set on an original (master) tape. Set to 0 if Master Tape contains no error. 1 if error occurred while reading a record from the Master Tape.
Analog-to-digital (AD) conversion resolution. Set to 0 for 12-bit AD resolution 1 for 8-bit AD resolution.
Flag indicating 'narrow-band, no compression' data (for compatibility with Mk III ODR). Set to 0001.
Last two digits of year, from Monitor and Control Subsystem (DMC) monitor data.

Flag indicating whether frequency synthesizer is in-lock. Set to 0 if frequency synthesizer is OUT-OF-LOCK 1 if frequency synthesizer is IN-LOCK*
Flag indicating whether limit enable is on. Set to 0 if limit enable is OFF* 1 if limit enable is ON
Flag indicating whether the tracking function is on. Set to 0 if track is OFF 1 if track is ON*
Flag indicating whether the acquisition function is on. Set to 0 if acquisition is OFF* 1 if acquisition is ON
Flag indicating whether the sweep function is on. Set to 0 if sweep is OFF 1 if sweep is ON*

Frequency read back from the POCA frequency registers in binary coded decimal (BCD); the best estimate of the POCA frequency at the time given in Field 14. BCD may be interpreted from hex as follows: Byte Hex 28 41 29-30 5624 31-32 2167 33-34 3152 Indicates a POCA frequency of 41,562,421.673152 Hz.

title: GLL Original Data Record RSC-11-11 File
pds:Table_Binary.pds:description: Original Data Records (ODRs) are raw data generated by the Deep Space Network Radio Science System. The raw data are samples of the output from one or more open-loop receivers. ODRs are defined here in terms of a PDS TABLE object, each record being represented as a row in the table. Each row in the table (record) contains a record header (166 bytes) and then a repeating structure of data samples. The number of bytes in each data structure and the number of structure repetitions per record depend on the sample rate and number of bits per sample. ODR formats have evolved slowly over the years, and continue to evolve; the structure described here corresponds to that documented by the DSN for tape delivery of data in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN RSC-11-11 DSN RADIO SCIENCE SYSTEM ORIGINAL DATA RECORD (ODR) AND ORIGINAL DATA STREAM (ODS) Several of the fields in the ODR contain information on sources and destinations for data, represented by numerical codes. These codes are defined by the DSN in DOCUMENT 820-13; REV. A DSN SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS DETAILED INTERFACE DESIGN OPS-6-8 DSN 1200-BIT AND 4800-BIT DATA BLOCK HEADER CODE ASSIGNMENTS, MARK IVA, 1985

Set to 0 if the time tag in Field 10 was generated by DSP-R software counting from the last Frequency and Timing Subsystem (FTS) 1-second pulse and configuration information in Fields 69 through 72 was copied forward by software and not read directly from the NBOC buffer. 1 if the time tag was from FTS and Fields 69 through 72 came directly from NBOC buffer.
